trajectory_summary: The agent inspected the provided template workbook (/root/data/test-rar.xlsx) and the source gold price workbook (/root/data/gold-prices.xlsx), extracted monthly gold prices for 2022M9–2023M9, then used openpyxl (turn 21) to populate Gold price!B2:B14 and add Excel formulas for log returns (col C) and rolling volatilities (cols D/E). It filled Answer step blocks: Step 1 (C3:C6), Step 2 (country list, 2023 gold values from Value plus Sweden converted from Volume using a 2023M* average price, and “exposure” formulas), and Step 3 (replicated Step 2 entries, attempted Total Reserves lookups, and computed RaR%). The output was saved as /root/output/rar_result.xlsx and verified to load (turn 23). However, the official feedback shows only 17/43 checks passed: gold reserve values were largely correct, but Step 1 volatility outputs (C4–C6), all Step 2 exposures, and all Step 3 total-reserves and RaR% calculations failed.
what_worked: Gold prices were successfully populated into the template: turn 22 shows Gold price rows 2–14 with numeric prices in column B (e.g., row 14 “2023M9”, 1915.434761904762).
The agent correctly identified the 2023 row and the set of countries with gold reserve VALUE data: turn 16 found year_row 18 and listed 8 countries with values (Austria…Finland).

It detected an additional Volume-only country (Sweden) and added it to Step 2: turn 17 shows Sweden present in Volume 2023 data, and turn 22 shows Sweden included in Answer row 11 with a value formula using Volume times AVERAGEIF over 2023M*.
The workbook output artifact was created and is readable: turn 23 lists /root/output/rar_result.xlsx and “Workbook load OK”.

issues.evidence: Turn 21 writes rolling volatility formulas as “STDEV.S(C{r-2}:C{r})” for 3-month (col D) and “STDEV.S(C{r-11}:C{r})” for 12-month (col E), and Answer formulas pull the “latest” from those columns (turn 22 shows Answer C4/C5/C6 formulas). Official feedback reports step1:C4 failed, step1:C5 failed, step1:C6 failed.
issues.cause: The volatility definition/annualization in the workbook does not match what the verifier expects (e.g., sample vs population stdev and/or missing/incorrect annualization conventions for the 3M and 12M series). Because C4–C6 are sourced from these computed volatility columns, the mismatch propagates directly into Step 1 answers.

issues.where: turn 21-22 (Step 2 exposure formulas in Answer row 13)
issues.evidence: Turn 22 shows exposure formulas like “=IF(C12="","",C12*$C$3*($C$5/100)*SQRT(3/12))” repeated across countries. Official feedback reports every step2:*:exposure test failed while the corresponding gold_value tests passed.
issues.cause: The exposure/VaR computation is formulaically inconsistent with the benchmark’s intended definition (likely using the wrong volatility input and/or applying an extra horizon scaling factor). Even with correct gold reserve values, this produces systematically incorrect exposures for all countries.

issues.where: turn 21-22 (Step 3 Total Reserves lookup and downstream RaR%)
issues.evidence: Turn 22 shows Step 3 total reserves formulas such as “=IFERROR(INDEX('Total Reserves'!$C:$P, MATCH(2023,'Total Reserves'!$A:$A,0), MATCH(C20&':*','Total Reserves'!$C$1:$P$1,0)),"")”. The rolling summary states the year appears as text “2023” in the IMF-style sheets. Official feedback reports all step3:*:total_reserves and step3:*:rar_percent tests failed.
issues.cause: The lookup uses MATCH(2023, ...) with a numeric year, but the sheet stores years as text “2023”, so the row MATCH fails and IFERROR masks this as blank totals. With missing denominators, RaR% calculations are also incorrect/blank, causing all Step 3 failures.

outcome_rationale: With official feedback showing 17/43 correct and failures in Step 1 volatility outputs, all Step 2 exposures, and all Step 3 total-reserves/RaR% computations, the produced workbook likely does not meet the task requirements.
